top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu) is my first choice on literary grounds under the common criteria. As I understand it from public knowledge and the shortlist description, he has a distinctive voice: dense, patterned prose that joins memory, the body, dream and cosmology in one imaginative system. His formal achievement lies in the cumulative architecture of Blinding (the first volume of the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid. The intellectual depth lies in an attempt to turn private perception into a cosmology. I would centre the citation on the prose project and treat the poetry as the source of its attention to the sentence, since the poetry is the thinnest-translated strand and I cannot confirm its weight. The preference remains provisional. I have not read the works or independently verified any source. Much of the effect is said to lie in Romanian rhythm and density, which I can judge only through translation. Whether the later long books deepen the project or restate its motifs is unresolved, and length alone is not sustained quality. Adonis remains a very close alternative on the linguistic renewal of a whole poetic language, and the gap reflects the committee's evidence more than a proven difference in merit. Nothing in the supplied evidence justifies preferring no award (P000) to a laureate, so P000 is ranked last.
recusal_note: none apparent from the profile. It records no personal or professional tie to Cărtărescu or any other shortlisted writer. My election alongside Ingrid Carlberg in 2020, and my Central European subject matter and years in Prague and Vienna, are context and not evidence of preference. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
